## Spring 2027 registration: the dates that matter

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
| When | What |
|---|---|
| Oct. 14 | Spring 2027 Schedule of Classes posted (already live in OSCAR) |
| **Oct. 29**, by 6:00 PM ET | Phase I **time tickets** post |
| Oct. 31, 11:59 PM ET | Last day to withdraw from a Fall 2026 course with a W |
| **Nov. 2 &ndash; Dec. 18** | **Phase I registration** |
| Jan. 4 &ndash; 15 | Phase II registration (schedule changes) |
| Jan. 15, 11:59 PM ET | Last day to drop a Spring course without a W |
:::

::: {.nonincremental style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
- Your **time ticket** is the earliest moment you can register. 
- Check it in OSCAR on Oct. 29 and clear any **holds** with your advisor.
:::

::: {.cite-note}
Source: [@registrar_calendar]
:::

::: notes
Dates from the Registrar's 2026&ndash;27 calendar (last updated October 19, 2026); re-check before
class. Time tickets are assigned by earned hours, so students with AP or dual-enrollment credit may
get earlier tickets than classmates. Remind them that a W does not affect GPA but does show on the
transcript, and that dropping below 12 hours can affect financial aid and scholarships; anyone
considering a withdrawal should talk to their advisor first. Spring classes start Jan. 11.
:::

## First priority: math and Physics I and II

Every upper-level Physics course waits on these chains. Register for the next course in each chain first, then build the rest of your schedule around them.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.nonincremental}
- **Math:** MATH 1551 &rarr; 1552 &rarr; 2551 &rarr; 2552
- **Physics I and II:** PHYS 2211 or 2231 &rarr; PHYS 2212 or 2232
- **Then** the major opens up: PHYS 2213 / 2303 / 2304 &rarr; 3000-level &rarr; 4000-level
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.highlight-box}
If something has to slip a semester, let it be an elective or a gen-ed, not a foundational course.
:::
:::
::::

These sections fill. Pick a backup section for each one before your time ticket opens.

::: notes
Callback to Lecture 4 (Building a Degree Plan): QM I needs PHYS 2213 or 2304 plus MATH 2551 and
2552, so a one-semester slip in calculus or Physics II pushes most of the major back a year.
Students who placed out of MATH 1551 or PHYS 2211 but felt shaky should raise it with their
advisor now. Check OSCAR for which spring sections are already near capacity.
:::

## Booking your academic advisor in Navigate360

::: {.nonincremental}
1. Log in at [gatech.navigate.eab.com](https://gatech.navigate.eab.com/) or the **Navigate360** app (GT login).
2. Open the **My Team** tab to see your assigned advisor.
3. Select **Schedule an Appointment**, choose advising, and pick a time.
:::

**Bring:** your Degree Map, a draft Spring schedule, and your questions.

School of Physics has its own career advisor: Dr. Sven Behrens

::: {.cite-note}
Source: [@gt_find_advisor; @physics_career]
:::

::: notes
Advisor names are from the Center for Academic Success "Find Your Advisor" page; confirm before
class, since My Team in Navigate360 is the authoritative assignment. A School of Physics faculty
member also counts for the assignment. If no slots are open before Oct. 30, students should email
their advisor (clear subject line, full name, major) and document the attempt. Consider having
everyone open Navigate360 on their phones right now.
:::
